text: What is Kestra? Now Kestra is an open source infinitely scalable orchestration platform that enables
all types of engineers to manage business critical workflows. Now why Kestra is a great choice for
workflow orchestration is because you can build your workflows as code, no code or with AI.
And you can do all three of these things interchangeably. You can start by building your workflow
in flow code. You can then transition to editing it with the no code editor. And then if you're not
sure about adding an extra bit of functionality at the end, you can go and ask the AI co-pilot to
add it for you. Kestra also has a humongous plugin library. When I say humongous, I mean over a
thousand dedicated plugins, which means you can connect Kestra to all of your favorite tools.
In this case, we're going to be connecting to things like Postgres, Google Cloud, as well as Python.
And on the topic of Python, Kestra is actually language agnostic. Some orchestration platforms are
only able to run Python, which is a great choice for a lot of use cases, but doesn't necessarily
mean it's always the right tool for the job. Being language agnostic means if you need performance,
you could use a language like Go or C. Whereas if you need something that's maybe quicker to be
able to write something together, then Python might be a good choice. And so having that option to
pick a language that's good for the job, rather than the one that your orchestration uses,
gives you a lot of options. And on top of all of this, Kestra gives you full visibility into your
workflows. With detailed logging, you can easily see what's going on in your workflows. You can set
up error-alerting too to notify you when things do go wrong, so you can jump in and fix them when
needed. And lastly, an orchestrator wouldn't be an orchestrator without the ability to manage how
your executions of your workflows start. Kestra has support for both schedule and event-based triggers,
which means you have the option to decide how these workflows start. Whether that's a nightly job
running overnight, or you have it set up where data arrives in your data lake or storage bucket,
and you can automatically start your workflows based on that. So with all of this combined,
this is what makes Kestra a fantastic choice for building data pipelines. And why we're going to
be using it for this module to build our very own ETL pipeline. Hopefully this has helped you
understand what makes Kestra different from other orchestration tools, or even just a traditional
cron job. In the next video inside of part two, I'm going to walk you through the various concepts
to build your own workflows inside of Kestra. So I'd make sure you check that out, and then we can
build our very first ETL pipeline.
